newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares advance on higher Wall St close.
newsitem.headline: German shares advance on higher Wall St close.

text.p: German shares advance in pre-bourse IBIS electronic trade early on Tuesday, with spirits lifted by an overnight advance on Wall Street and sentiment underpinned by a stable dollar.
By 0726 GMT the IBIS DAX index was up 54.26 points at 4,134.81 points, a rise of 1.33 percent, while the September DAX future contract was up 55.5 points at 4,142 points.
"We expected it to turn around at some point and now I think we should keep going. No one is long as everyone was caught by surprise by the move when it happened," a Frankfurt broker said.
Conditions in the market were favourable, he said.
"The fact that the Bundesbank left the repo unchanged means there is no sign of a rate move," he said.
"Volumes are pretty thin at the moment, but I reckon that when they do come in to the market, they will be on the buy side," the broker said.

The biggest gainer in early trade was Volkswagen AG, which was up 4.33 percent at 1,338.50 marks. The group was in favour after it said on German television late on Monday that it expected to sell around 700,000 of its new Golf vehicles in the first year.
The dollar, which has lost a considerable amount of ground against the mark in recent days, picked up slightly and was stable in the run-up to German bourse trade.
The German banks notably picked up after incurring heavy losses in the previous days.
Commerzbank was up 1.84 marks -- a rise of 2.87 percent -- to 65.85 marks and was the most heavily-traded stock in IBIS trade.
Deutsche Bank also picked up, rising 2.15 marks to 113.50 marks, with the other member of the banking triumvirate, Dresdner, up 1.35 marks at 79.20.
Also higher early was pharmaceutical group Merck KGaA which rose by 2.85 percent to 70.45 marks in advance of its half-year figures expected on Wednesday.
Chemical group Bayer AG, last of the Big Three to report its interim figures, fell 0.55 percent to 69.90 marks in advance of its figures.
